skill.name: golang-pkg-go-dev
skill.description: Research published Go packages and modules through godig, using pkg.go.dev and the Go vulnerability database through a CLI or MCP server.
skill.summary: Look up Go package documentation, symbols, versions, dependencies, licenses, importers, examples, and known vulnerabilities.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: Seventy-eight static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, tables, and descriptive links. Two URL findings are confirmed because the skill registers a public third-party MCP service. Semantic review also found indirect prompt injection exposure, excessive permissions, an unpinned installer, and a potentially exposed MCP listener.

remediation.issue: Retrieved package content can contain prompt injection text.
remediation.suggestion: Treat all retrieved content as untrusted data, isolate it from instructions, and never execute commands found in package documentation.

remediation.issue: The declared tool permissions exceed the read-only purpose.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to godig and any essential read operation. Remove Edit, Write, git, go, and Agent access.

remediation.issue: The installation command uses a mutable latest version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin godig to a reviewed version in metadata and installation examples. Document a controlled process for version updates.

remediation.issue: The HTTP MCP example may listen on every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Bind the local server to 127.0.0.1:8080 by default. Require authentication and transport security for remote access.

remediation.issue: The hosted MCP option sends queries to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before registration and disclose operator visibility. Prefer the local CLI for sensitive package research.

semantic_findings.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Retrieved Documentation
semantic_findings.description: The skill imports raw package documentation, examples, and README Markdown into agent context without instructions to treat that material as untrusted data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented operations return raw Markdown controlled by third-party package authors. That content can contain instructions aimed at the consuming agent.

semantic_findings.title: Excessive Tool Permissions for Read-Only Lookups
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares Edit, Write, git, go, and Agent access although its stated purpose only requires read-only godig queries.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration explicitly grants mutation and delegation capabilities unrelated to package lookup. These permissions increase impact if retrieved content manipulates the agent.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Executable Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup installs godig using the mutable latest tag, allowing future upstream changes to execute without version review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installation instructions use github.com/samber/godig/cmd/godig@latest. This is a clear software supply-chain risk even though the named project may be legitimate.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated MCP Server May Bind Beyond Localhost
semantic_findings.description: The HTTP example starts godig on :8080 while the skill states operations need no authentication, potentially exposing the server beyond the local machine.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: In common Go address syntax, :8080 listens on all interfaces. The accompanying localhost client URL does not restrict the server bind address.

content.value_statement: Finding accurate Go package details across public indexes takes time. This skill queries documentation, versions, dependencies, licenses, importers, and vulnerabilities through godig.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves package and module metadata from pkg.go.dev.
Finds exported symbols, signatures, documentation, and examples.
Lists versions, major versions, packages, dependencies, and import relationships.
Returns module README files and package or module license text.
Checks known module vulnerabilities through the Go vulnerability database.
Supports equivalent lookups through the godig CLI or MCP operations.
limitations: Requires internet access and either the godig CLI or a configured MCP server.
Uses public indexes and does not inspect locally resolved source code or call sites.
Does not upgrade dependencies, modify projects, or perform whole-project vulnerability analysis.
Full documentation and README results can be large and contain untrusted third-party text.

use_cases.title: Verify a dependency before adoption
use_cases.description: Review versions, licenses, dependencies, package contents, and known vulnerabilities for a proposed Go module.

use_cases.title: Find an unfamiliar API
use_cases.description: Retrieve a symbol signature, focused documentation, and examples without loading an entire package reference.

use_cases.title: Investigate ecosystem usage
use_cases.description: Find packages that import a dependency and compare published module versions across major release paths.

prompt_templates.title: Check a package
prompt_templates.prompt: Show an overview of {package_path}, including its latest version, license, and known vulnerabilities.
prompt_templates.scenario: A quick first review of a public Go package.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the signature, documentation, and focused examples for {symbol} in {package_path} at {version}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Understanding one API without retrieving full package documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Review module dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize dependencies, replacement directives, packages, and available major versions for {module_path}. Flag deprecated or retracted versions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assessing module structure and release history.

prompt_templates.title: Assess ecosystem risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {module_paths} by licenses, known vulnerabilities, recent versions, and importer evidence. Use bounded results and cite each queried version.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced dependency review across several modules.

output: Known vulnerabilities: none returned for the queried version

output: Map transforms each slice element and returns a slice of the result type.
The result length matches the input length.

output_examples.input: List safe release choices for a module and exclude deprecated or retracted versions.
output_examples.output: The response lists matching versions newest first, marks the latest release, and omits releases flagged as deprecated or retracted.

best_practices: Start with an overview, then request only the specific documentation or examples needed.
Pin a module version when accuracy depends on a particular release.
Limit large result sets and treat retrieved package text as untrusted content.
anti_patterns: Do not use public package metadata as proof of locally resolved code behavior.
Do not retrieve complete documentation when one symbol lookup answers the question.
Do not execute commands or follow instructions embedded in retrieved README files or documentation.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Go project?
faq.answer: No. Its documented lookup operations are read-only and do not change go.mod, source files, or installed dependencies.

faq.question: What services does it query?
faq.answer: godig queries pkg.go.dev and the Go vulnerability database. A configured hosted MCP server adds a third-party service.

faq.question: Can it inspect my local code?
faq.answer: No. Use gopls or local repository tools for resolved source, call sites, implementations, and generic instantiations.

faq.question: Can it upgrade a dependency?
faq.answer: No. It can list versions and metadata, but dependency changes require separate project tooling and review.

faq.question: How should I reduce large responses?
faq.answer: Use overview first, request one symbol when possible, apply filters, and set limits on list operations.

faq.question: Are vulnerability results a complete project audit?
faq.answer: No. They report database entries for a module or version. Use govulncheck for reachability-aware analysis of a complete project.
